text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy said on Wednesday it expected its full-year 1996 profit after financial items to exceed the 1995 level and net sales to reach almost 12 billion markka.

"The profit after net financial items will increase from 1995 due to the effect of non-recurring items," Metra said in a statement with its January-August results. "Metra's net sales for 1996 are estimated to reach almost 12 billion markka," it said.
Metra's 1995 profit after financial items totalled 795 million markka on net sales of 10.62 billion.
Metra said full-year net sales at its biggest division, Wartsila Diesel, were expected to exceed eight billion markka compared to 6.92 billion in 1995.
"The profit after net financial items should stand at last year's level," Metra said, referring to the diesel engine manufacturing business group.

Bathroom ceramics maker Sanitec was expected to show full-year net sales of 2.6 billion markka, up from 2.5 billion in 1995. The unit's 1996 profit after net financial items "should come close to the strong level in 1995," Metra said.

Imatra Steel's net sales for the year would be around 900 million markka, down from 994 million in 1995. "The profit after net financial items is expected to be satisfactory but well down on the record level in 1995," Metra said.
